explain.say: Have you ever had a worry that buzzes round your head like a fly? Here is a trick to give it somewhere to go. Look at the board. This is how a worry box works.

explain.say: See the cloud? Notice a worry. A worry is a thought that keeps buzzing, like, What if I get my spelling wrong? Everyone has worries. Can you think of one small worry you have?

explain.say: Next, see the pencil? Draw or write the worry on a small piece of paper. Then fold it up small. Putting it on paper takes it out of your head for a while. What would you draw?

explain.say: Now it goes into the box. The box holds the worry for you, so your head can rest. Later, you open the box with a grown-up and talk about it together. Who would you open it with?

explain.say: Important! Some things go in the box: a spelling test, a tricky game, a new club. But some you tell a grown-up straight away: someone hurt me, I feel unsafe, I am lost. Well done! Your challenge: decorate a worry box.

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Box now, or tell a grown-up now?

faq.a: A worry is a thought about something that might go wrong, like a test or a new place. Everyone has worries sometimes.
asks: Tell me about Notice a worry

faq.q: Why does a worry box help?
faq.a: Putting the worry on paper and in the box gives your head a rest. You know it is safe, and you will talk about it later.
asks: Tell me about Into the box

faq.a: You open the box with a grown-up you trust, like a parent or teacher. Together you talk about each worry.

faq.q: Which worries should I tell a grown-up straight away?
faq.a: If someone hurts you, if you feel unsafe, if you are lost, or if someone is being mean, tell a grown-up you trust straight away. Do not wait for the box.
asks: Tell me about Tell a grown-up now

faq.q: How do I make a worry box?
faq.a: Use a small box with a lid, like a shoe box. Decorate it, and cut a slot in the top. Keep paper and a pencil nearby.

facts: Writing a worry down can help it feel smaller.
Worry dolls from Guatemala are a tradition: children tell their worries to tiny dolls at bedtime.
